project.title: Cellular Soft Robots
project.manuscript: A monolithic cellular architecture for topology-programmable soft robotics

items.title: cell/module split
items.detail: Sweep the whole manuscript so cell, module, array, layer, and topology are never used interchangeably; keep the current definition near Methods and echo it in Results captions where the reader first needs it.

items.title: flexural-joint wording
items.detail: Replace claims that imply a discrete flexural hinge with compliant-linkage language; name the Sarrus legs as bending beams and state what actually bends under inflation.

items.title: overhang endpoint definition
items.detail: Define exactly where the approximately 1 cm overhang starts and ends; add the same reference endpoints in text, caption, and figure annotation.

items.title: overhang reference lines
items.detail: Add vertical dashed reference lines or a bracket to the overhang figure so the measurement is visible without reading the paragraph first.

items.title: single-cell mechanism
items.detail: Separate cell-level expansion from module-level bending: cell equals monolithic Sarrus-linkage-plus-PneuNet unit; module equals the 2 by 2 pneumatic grouping.

items.title: upper/lower leg asymmetry
items.detail: Describe the upper thin structural legs and lower thicker pneumatic-channel legs as the source of directional bias, using the upright-V and inverted-V language already visible in the figure.

items.title: print-reliability hinge note
items.detail: Explain that an intentional notch-like hinge was not used because many cells must print reliably and unsupported thin hinge features become floppy or unreliable at higher layers.

items.title: simulation-language cleanup
items.detail: Do not imply the current physical cell matches an ideal rigid-link/flexible-joint model; state where the real compliant beams and distributed bending depart from that abstraction.

items.title: module-bias evidence
items.detail: Tie the 80 psi side views, angle plot, and V-shaped leg-pair annotations to one explicit claim: asymmetric connection geometry converts in-plane expansion into repeatable convex bending.

items.title: stiffness paragraph bridge
items.detail: Connect the force-stiffness regimes to the same beam-bending story: early axial resistance, low-stiffness leg bending, and high-stiffness pneumatic-chamber compression.

items.title: overhang requirement
items.detail: State the requirement in physical terms: curvature relative to thickness, available length, local expansion ratio, boundary constraint, and the ability to generate both convex and concave bending.

items.title: threshold question
items.detail: Add a short calculation or design-rule paragraph that answers what combination of curvature, length, thickness, and expansion makes an overhang possible.

items.title: 66-cell limit
items.detail: Make the current prototype boundary explicit: 33-cell row, two opposed layers, 66 total cells, about 1 cm overhang, proof-of-principle row rather than a full two-dimensional overhang surface.

items.title: boundary-condition role
items.detail: State whether the boundary helps or limits the overhang; if edge constraints are part of the effect, put that in the figure/caption instead of leaving it implicit.

items.title: expansion-ratio reality
items.detail: Clarify that constrained modules may not reach the ideal 2x expansion in the deformed structure; relate leakage, actuation strength, and compression to the achieved overhang.

items.title: node/mesh analysis
items.detail: Create a simple node-following or mesh analysis from planar state to overhang state so stretch, local bend, and length demand can be inspected rather than argued verbally.

items.title: avoid water analogy drift
items.detail: Keep the overhang comparison focused on material deformation without molecular rearrangement; do not let the analogy carry the evidence.

items.title: do not abandon pneumatics
items.detail: Keep pneumatics as the current proven platform; frame EPMs first as valve/manifold control for cells rather than as a replacement actuation system without hard range data.

items.title: manifold architecture
items.detail: Sketch or describe one pressure manifold feeding many cells, with each cell controlled by a small electrically switched EPM valve.

items.title: direct magnetic actuation boundary
items.detail: If direct EPM actuation remains in the Discussion, mark it as a separate future path that requires range, force, scale, and heating evidence before it can replace air.

items.title: physical EPM switching test
items.detail: Run a minimal test with Alnico and NdFeB rods in a tube or constrained guide, measuring attraction/repulsion switching and whether the soft magnet twists.

items.title: pulse circuit note
items.detail: Describe the EPM as pulse-switched between stable states; avoid treating it like a continuously powered electromagnet or solenoid.

items.title: student overlap
items.detail: Capture the relevant magnetic-soft-actuator student connection and the split-magnet EPM concept if it becomes a real cited design input.

items.title: one claim per figure
items.detail: For each main figure, write the single claim the figure proves; remove panels or caption phrases that do not support that claim.

items.title: large readable labels
items.detail: Increase angle markers, reference lines, pressure labels, and panel lettering so they remain legible at printed caption scale.

items.title: cell figure
items.detail: Make Figure 1 distinguish uncapped cell, capped cell, Sarrus linkage, PneuNet actuator, and cap role without mixing module behavior into the cell caption.

items.title: module figure
items.detail: Make Figure 2 carry the directional-bias mechanism: upper/lower leg pairs, single-module and two-module bending angles, and the unactuated cross-section.

items.title: overhang figure
items.detail: Add measurement references, layer labels, actuation pattern, cell count, and physical row state so the 1 cm claim is visually checkable.

items.title: cylindrical figures
items.detail: Make bending, grasping, peristalsis, and rolling panels read as topology-level reconfiguration of the same module, not a separate actuator family.

items.title: source consistency
items.detail: Check every caption number against the exported figures: pressure, expansion ratio, cell count, module count, angle, overhang length, and topology size.

items.title: title
items.detail: Make the title contribution-bearing and concrete; avoid a broad category title unless the Results prove that breadth.

items.title: abstract arc
items.detail: Open with problem, approach, strongest real result, main limitation, and bounded claim; remove repeated topology-programmable language that does not add evidence.

items.title: novelty sentence
items.detail: State the exact novelty over programmable matter, fixed soft surfaces, and modular soft robots: one printed pneumatic unit used for both morphing surfaces and reconfigurable robot bodies.

items.title: Results order
items.detail: Lead each Results subsection with evidence and measured behavior, not a tour of what was built.

items.title: quantitative spine
items.detail: Add a compact chain of hard numbers: pressure range, expansion ratio, stiffness regimes, bending angles, feature height, overhang length, load/object interaction, locomotion outcome, and repeat count where available.

items.title: claim discipline
items.detail: Keep claims bounded to demonstrated prototypes; do not overstate autonomy, closed-loop control, integrated valves, sensing, or full two-dimensional overhang surfaces.

items.title: comparison paragraph
items.detail: Compare against the closest systems in the Introduction and Discussion using direct capability differences, not only citation lists.

items.title: limitations paragraph
items.detail: Make limitations crisp: external pressure, tubing, manual assembly, scale, speed, leakage, limited overhang prototype, no closed-loop control, and no integrated EPM valve yet.

items.title: Methods reproducibility
items.detail: Add enough detail for fabrication, materials, print orientation, pressure control, measurement calibration, boundary conditions, and analysis scripts to be audited.

items.title: editorial package
items.detail: Prepare the Science cover-letter line, graphical claim, suggested reviewers, competing-work comparison, and data/code availability before submission.
